newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: East Europe stock markets surge but slowdown seen.
newsitem.headline: East Europe stock markets surge but slowdown seen.

text.p: Most east European stock markets were in bullish mood this week but dealers were generally less confident about strong growth prospects in the short and medium term.
Warsaw, Prague, and Bucharest posted year-highs while Slovenia's SBI index stunned investors by hitting an all-time high on Monday and then plunging by nearly one fifth over the next four sessions.
The CESI Central European Share Index fell by 0.58 percent on the week to 1,710.45.
WARSAW

Polish shares crossed the 18,000 point threshold on Friday, setting a third straight 34-month high, and analysts said that stronger buying after the price-fixing signalled that the recent foreign buying frenzy could continue into next week.
"It seems to me that next week can be very similar to this though for about two weeks there's been no fundamental reason for that to happen," said Tomasz Berent, an analyst at IB Austria Securities.
Some analysts said growth could slow next week with some investors taking profits. The market rose 719.3 points, or 4.1 percent this week putting it 36.8 percent up from mid-December.

They said two of the week's main market top gainers, Budimex which rose 34.8 percent and Elektromontaz Export which was up 23.5 percent, could be gaining on anticipation of good earnings data by construction firms during this year's warm January.
Most listed firms release January data early next week.
PRAGUE
The PX50 posted a two-year high of 603.0 at mid-week but slipped back slightly on Thursday and Friday on fears that major issues may have risen too high, too fast.
By the end of the week, the PX50 was virtually unchanged from Monday's open, edging up 0.2 percent to 601.1.

Despite continued strength in blue chips, dealers warned that recent gains had been made on generally low volumes. In the absence of new information on company fundamentals they were sceptical about the shares' short-term prospects.
"I would expect that the prices of the blue chips are going to go down during the next week but probably not by much," said Ivan Kusacek of Zivnostenska Banka.
BUDAPEST
The Budapest Stock Exchange's BUX index fell two percent on Friday following the release of a mixed bag of corporate results, traders said.
On Friday the BUX closed at 5,520.40 points, down 136.93 from last Friday.

The market had been waiting nervously for oil and gas company MOL's 1996 results but the better-than-expected figures failed to make up for other companies' disappointing performances, notably chemicals maker TVK.
LJUBLJANA
The Slovenian SBI index slumped after hitting an all-time high on Monday of 1,655.4. By Friday the index was 17 percent below Monday's opening level.

Traders said the fall was caused by a central bank decree forcing foreign portfolio investors to trade through special custody or fiduciary accounts opened at any of Slovenia's 14 fully-licensed banks.
BRATISLAVA
The SAX index on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) continued to grow this week, boosted mainly by strong foreign demand. The 16-share index rose 3.6 percent throughout the week.

"We think that the current strong demand from foreign investors should keep the market running up for some time, and that the SAX can even break the 200-point level in the foreseeable future," said Libor Briska of Creditanstalt.
BUCHAREST
With major issue Azomures absent from the Bucharest Stock Exchange, buying interest focused on other stocks, sending most prices higher and pushing its two unofficial indices to year highs.

Turnover climbed to an all-time high of 6.3 billion lei early in the week on heavy trading in fertiliser maker Azomures, but sagged on Thursday to 112 million with the stock suspended after a share split.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks ended a generally jittery week on a positive note as trade livened up on Friday and blue chips were expected to lead a slow market recovery in the days ahead.
Foreign investors, whose interest has supported a Zagreb bourse bull run, seemed to have overcome their nervousness about trade controls imposed in nearby Slovenia, analysts said.
"I foresee mild growth for liquid stocks from the beginning of next week," said Davor Relja of Faktor brokerage.
